clue.text: Acceptable feature on a headdress for a friar

parts.note: a cap is a simple headdress
U is the old abbreviation for upper-class, hence socially acceptable
the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: Something proper is to be found on a holy man's head covering.
explanation.walkthrough: A Capuchin is a Franciscan friar, the order named for its pointed hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capuchins are an order of Franciscan monks, each member being a friar.

clue.text: Biblical cephalopod?

explanation.surface: A squid-like creature from the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ammonites were a people of the Old Testament; an ammonite is also a fossil shelled mollusc related to the squid and octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a member of the tribe descended from Ammon in Genesis; the other a coiled fossil mollusc of the cephalopod class.

clue.text: Those PR rules confused the furnishers

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Publicity guidelines baffled the people fitting out the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the twelve letters of THOSE PR RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholsterers pad and cover chairs and sofas, so they furnish rooms with soft furniture.

clue.text: Is the runner a ringer? It's certainly a plant

parts.note: a hare is a fast runner
a bell rings, so it is a ringer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the athlete is an impostor and is told it is certainly planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringer' suggests an impostor and 'plant' a spy, but the ringer is a bell and the plant is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a wild flower with blue bell-shaped blooms, a member of the plant kingdom.

clue.text: A negative account this, as the Roman said of the first sailor

parts.note: no is a negative reply
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: A Roman refuses an account of the earliest seafarer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sailor is Noah of the Ark; 'Noachic' is the adjective meaning to do with Noah.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark and sailed it through the Flood, so the adjective for things relating to him describes the first mariner.

clue.text: Many occur in rings and cycles

definitions.text: Many occur in rings and cycles

parts.words: Many occur in rings and cycles
parts.note: suggests flower parts arranged in whorls, but means the foot levers of bicycles and of bell-like organ keyboards

explanation.surface: Many things turn up in circles and recurring patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' are bicycles, each with a pair of foot-operated levers; 'rings' plays on circles of petals, a near-sound the clue invites.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicycles are driven by foot levers turned in a circle, so these parts occur on every cycle.

clue.text: Spanish agreement about measure for the House

indicators.note: about means around, so the Spanish yes goes round the measure

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A Spaniard agrees on a measure to put before Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' looks like Parliament but is a type of dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house shares one wall with its neighbour, and is commonly shortened in Britain.

clue.text: Intimidate the Tories in wet part of Cambs

indicators.note: in means the right is placed inside the fen

parts.note: Cambridgeshire (Cambs) is famous for its fens, low marshy land
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: Conservatives in the Cambridgeshire marshes try to bully people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat drained marshland of eastern England, much of it in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten someone is to scare or cow them, which is what intimidation does.

clue.text: Eavesdrop, like many war-time GI's. say

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: American soldiers in wartime Britain were famously 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'

explanation.surface: Many American soldiers in the war listened in, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime British gibe about US troops was 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'; OVER HERE spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen in secretly and catch words not meant for you.

clue.text: Nurse a retired actor

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for actor is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: Someone looks after an actor who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the word for a poor actor backwards; 'Nurse' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nursemaid or maid in parts of East and South Asia.

clue.text: It's asking too much of the church organ giver, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A donor of a church organ is being asked for too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CH with ORGAN GIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcharging is demanding an excessive price, that is, wanting more payment than is fair.

clue.text: Hamlet's school friend finds Association opponents hard

parts.note: a guild is an association of craftsmen or merchants
E and N, East and North, are opposing partnerships at bridge
stern means hard or severe

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean student meets tough rivals from a club.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so E and N sit as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosencrantz's companion, sent for by Claudius, is a former fellow student of the Danish prince at Wittenberg.

clue.text: Paper, the first of the edition

indicators.note: the first of means only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: an issue is one edition of a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: A newspaper's first printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first of' takes T from 'the'; 'Paper' wants to be a newspaper but is tissue paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, used for wrapping or blowing one's nose.

clue.text: Charged in a street in Connecticut

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street
taken as written
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: Someone was charged on a road in a New England state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests an arrest, but means filled, as in 'instinct with life'.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct as an adjective means imbued or filled with a quality, so a scene instinct with menace is laden with it.

clue.text: Revokes engineers changes

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
deals are exchanges or transactions

explanation.surface: Army engineers' alterations are cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: At cards, a deal that has gone wrong is cancelled and replaced by a fresh one, so the setter equates a redeal with a revocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing the cards again undoes and annuls the previous deal, as revoking cancels something.

clue.text: Being in debt is a mistake — you have failed again

indicators.note: being in means the mistake sits inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Getting into debt is an error, and you have gone wrong once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' means owing money, so RED is the debt that holds LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a former bad state, failing once more after recovery.

clue.text: Cooking pot ran cold maybe

indicators.note: maybe means possibly, signalling the letters could form some other word

explanation.surface: A cooking pot went cold, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RAN COLD; this is the older spelling of cauldron.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron, here in its variant spelling, is a large pot for boiling food over a fire.

clue.text: This — — to thine own self be true" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: This — — to thine own self be true" (Hamlet)

parts.words: This — — to thine own self be true" (Hamlet)
parts.note: a quotation with two words missing, from Polonius's advice to his son Laertes

explanation.walkthrough: Polonius's line in Hamlet runs 'This above all: to thine own self be true'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words complete Polonius's line, meaning more than anything else, chiefly.

clue.text: Ways of escape round the old guard, away from the centre

indicators.note: round means the ways of escape go around the old word for guard

parts.note: outs are ways out of a difficulty
ward in an old sense means guard or guardianship

explanation.surface: Escape routes encircle the veteran sentries, leading away from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old guard' looks like the conservative faction, but means the archaic word for guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwards means towards the outside, moving off from the middle.

clue.text: Add about six points, as recommended

indicators.note: about means around, so the word add goes round the numeral and points

parts.note: taken as written
VI is six in Roman numerals
S and E, south and east, are compass points

explanation.surface: Add about six points, as was suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the first word of the clue around the numeral and the two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Advised means counselled or suggested, as a course of action someone urged.

clue.text: Authorized to burn spice in the cover

indicators.note: in means the incense word goes inside the cover word

parts.note: a lid is a cover
to cense is to perfume with burning incense

explanation.surface: Someone has permission to burn spices under a covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the old verb for perfuming with incense inside the cover; 'burn spice' looks like cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensed means granted official permission, so a licensed act is one that has been sanctioned.

clue.text: Deity represented by Burlington House?

parts.note: Burlington House in London is home to the Royal Academy, abbreviated RA, which is also the name of the Egyptian god of the sun

explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly in London houses the Royal Academy of Arts, whose initials RA name the Egyptian solar deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ra is the Egyptian solar deity, so the god he is stands for the sun.

clue.text: Fancy arranging tea with Ron

indicators.note: arranging means putting into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ron fancies setting out the tea things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges TEA with RON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what fancy means as an adjective.

clue.text: Foreboding here about quarter day, perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for here goes round the other pieces

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
N, north, is one quarter of the compass
a day is an example of a period of time

explanation.surface: A sense of doom arrives around one of the year's quarter days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter day' looks like a single term, the British rent day, but splits into a compass quarter and a period of time, which 'about' puts inside the word for here.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive feeling that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: The sin of the love-lorn messenger

indicators.note: lorn means bereft, so the messenger is without the love letter

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: The sin of a lovesick messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-lorn' looks like lovesick but means without love: O (zero) is taken from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins, the resentful wanting of what others have.

clue.text: Colour of eastern wine-producing area

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or wine-growing area

explanation.surface: The shade of a vineyard in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade, that of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Odysseus's wife, with no start, receives victory sign and wins jacket

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the letter goes inside the shortened name
with no start means the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Penelope was the faithful wife of Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey
V for victory is the famous sign made with two fingers

explanation.surface: Odysseus's wife, without a head start, gets a victory salute and wins a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and wins' adds nothing to the wordplay; it rounds off the surface. A jacket here is a cover for a letter or record.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket can be a paper cover or wrapper, which is what an envelope is for a letter.

clue.text: Stupid Head's banality

parts.note: dull means slow-witted or stupid
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A dim headteacher's triteness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a school head but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banality is a lack of originality or interest, the quality of being tedious and flat.
